race_context: North Harrison Community School Corp. serves the northern part of Harrison County; its board meets in the North Harrison Middle School cafeteria in Ramsey {cd_stifel}{cd_pay}. Superintendent Tim LaGrange, hired June 30, 2025 after six years leading Southwest Dubois County schools and two years at Kittitas School District in Washington state, replaced Nathan Freed, who left for South Harrison {cd_hire}{cd_search}. LaGrange has described North Harrison as a '$25 million annual school organization' {cd_stifel}.

Enrollment: LaGrange said in October 2025 that the corporation had 23 fewer students than the year before and 93 fewer than four years earlier, which he put at roughly $771,000 in lost state funding; the teachers' contract covers about 125 teachers {cd_pay}. A total enrollment figure was not found in fetched sources.

The board has five members, elected by township seat or at large {cd_search}{hc_2022}{hc_2024}: Josh Bowen (president), Angie Byrne (vice president, Morgan Township seat), Chris Bowyer (secretary), Kristina Gunter (at large) and Steve Nix (Blue River Township seat) {cd_stifel}{hc_2024}{cd_bowyer}. Voters in every North Harrison precinct vote in each township race {hc_gen_list}.

Three seats are on the 2026 ballot, one member each: At Large, Jackson Township and Spencer Township {hc_gen_list}{hc_sample_jackson}. In 2022 Gunter won the at-large seat, Chris Lasley the Jackson Township seat and Joshua Bowen the Spencer Township seat {hc_2022}. Bowyer, appointed to the board in September 2024 to fill a vacancy left by a resignation, is running in the Jackson Township race {cd_bowyer}{hc_gen_list}. Bowen, who won the Spencer Township seat in 2022, is running in the at-large race and describes it as a run for re-election {hc_2022}{cd_bowen}; Gunter is not on the 2026 ballot {hc_gen_list}. Josh Kendall is unopposed for the Spencer Township seat {hc_gen_list}{cd_gencands}.

Ballot changes: Ray Von Allmen, listed as a Republican at-large candidate on the state list, was removed as a candidate on Sept. 1, 2026 after a challenge to his candidacy filed by Alfred Wood, according to the Corydon Democrat {cd_atlarge}. The county's general-election candidate list and sample ballot show only Bowen and Ashley Black in the at-large race {hc_gen_list}{hc_sample_jackson}. Ashley Black appears with no party; the state list shows her as nonpartisan {hc_gen_list}{in_list}.

Budget and state funding (Oct. 2025): the board introduced a 2026 budget with an $18 million education fund, a $7 million operations fund and a $3.02 million debt service fund; the Corydon Democrat reported that the 2025 state budget would cut an estimated $381,730 from North Harrison for 2026 and that the corporation would again have to pay for school resource officers, which Harrison County had covered in 2025 {cd_pay}.

Finances (Jan. 2026): on Jan. 8 the board unanimously hired Stifel to do a financial analysis and five- to 10-year projections, after the corporation paid about $780,000 in health insurance claims in late 2025; the board also voted, with only Steve Nix opposed, to allow moving up to 15% of the education fund to the operations fund {cd_stifel}.

2027 budget (Sept. 10, 2026 hearing): LaGrange presented a proposed 2027 education fund of $17,454,909 (down from $18 million), an operations fund of $7.6 million and debt service of $2,951,137; the advertised operations tax rate is 0.6944 and the debt service rate 0.4266 {cd_crash}.

Teacher pay and contract: more than 10 teachers, parents and students urged higher teacher pay at the Oct. 16, 2025 meeting, when the corporation's offer was a $120,000 total increase; board member Bowyer said the money was not there to pay teachers more {cd_pay}. Teachers' union leaders also objected in June 2025 to the new superintendent's contract terms {cd_hire}. The teachers' contract expired June 30, 2026, according to candidate Ashley Black, and a collective bargaining public hearing was held Sept. 10, 2026 {cd_pushback}{cd_crash}.

Classroom display policy (July–Aug. 2026): the board unanimously approved a policy treating classroom displays as instructional materials and barring employees from posting materials that convey 'a political, religious, or personal message'; first reading passed July 24 and final reading Aug. 13 {cd_pushback}{cd_display}. Several teachers, residents and a student spoke against it, and the Corydon Democrat reported that no board member explained publicly why the policy was needed {cd_pushback}{cd_display}.

Student safety (Sept. 2026): at the Sept. 10 meeting, parents of middle school volleyball players criticized the district's response to an Aug. 26 crash involving the team bus on I-265; board members apologized, and LaGrange said, 'we can do better' {cd_crash}. The board also hired a special education consultant to audit services and staffing {cd_crash}.

Forums: no candidate forum was found. The Corydon Democrat (and its Clarion News edition) published questionnaire answers from the at-large and Jackson Township candidates in September 2026 {cd_atlarge}{cd_jackson}. Key differences in the Jackson Township race: Bowyer is the appointed incumbent and says the current board is making progress; Schenck, a former superintendent, criticizes district management and proposes about $500,000 in savings; Inboden and Fanz, first-time candidates, emphasize finances and academics {cd_bowyer}{cd_schenck}{cd_inboden}{cd_fanz}.

candidates.summary: Certified public accountant and 2004 North Harrison graduate making her second run for the board; says her priorities are a teachers' contract, finances and transparency {cd_black}. Listed without a party {hc_gen_list}.
background: Licensed CPA with a bachelor's degree in accounting and a master's in strategic finance; says she has more than 20 years of experience in accounting and finance {cd_black}.
Says she began attending board meetings in late 2019 to advocate for more special education resources, particularly at the elementary schools {cd_black}.
Ran for the Blue River Township seat in 2024, finishing fourth of five candidates {cd_black}{hc_2024}.
path_to_ballot: Filed for the at-large seat; appears on the county list with no party and on the state list as nonpartisan {hc_gen_list}{in_list}.

items: Says her immediate priority is for teachers and the board to reach an agreed master contract, and that it would be her 'focal point' until resolved {cd_black}.
In June 2025 public comment, urged the board to find ways to keep staff leaving for neighboring districts {cd_search}.
Says SEA 1 reduces funding to public schools and that the board needs members who can review financial statements closely {cd_black}.
Wants to find new revenue and cost savings that do not cut teacher and student resources, and to spend savings on things that add value to students' education {cd_black}.
Says the board should explain every vote and major decision, make public documents easier to get, and post meeting notices widely with supporting documents attached {cd_black}.

Opposed the 2026 classroom display policy, calling it too vague and saying more important issues faced the corporation, such as the expired teachers' contract and teacher retention {cd_pushback}{cd_display}.

on_incumbent: At the Aug. 13, 2026 meeting, said she disagreed with the classroom display policy and asked board members to explain their votes {cd_display}.
Said in July 2026 that teacher retention has been a continuing issue she has raised for seven years {cd_pushback}.
plans: Says she would bring 'strong financial oversight' to the board and keep asking where tax dollars go {cd_black}.
gaps: No endorsements or campaign finance reports found.
No candidate forum found; positions come from her newspaper questionnaire and public comments at board meetings.

candidates.summary: Incumbent board member and board president; elected to the Spencer Township seat in 2022 and now running at large {hc_2022}{cd_bowen}{cd_stifel}. Listed as a Republican {hc_gen_list}.
background: Worked at the Kroger distribution center in Louisville from 1992 to 2017, moving from order selector to a facility manager {cd_bowen}.
Board president for two years after serving one year as secretary; named president again for 2026 {cd_bowen}{cd_stifel}.
Member of the Harrison County Parks Inclusive Playground Advisory Board since 2019 {cd_bowen}.
Parent of a current North Harrison High School student {cd_bowen}.
path_to_ballot: Filed for the at-large seat as a Republican {hc_gen_list}{in_list}.

items: Names staffing, pay, benefits, morale and retention as his top priority; says wages and benefits must stay competitive and the teachers' contract must be fair to educators and keep the corporation solvent {cd_bowen}.
Wants to maintain enrollment and grow the district's new virtual school program for families who prefer non-traditional options {cd_bowen}.
Wants to expand special education services so all students can learn {cd_bowen}.
Supports building career-ready pathways through North Harrison career and technical programs and the Prosser Career Education Center {cd_bowen}.
Wants to modernize the athletic department, facilities and processes, and says he would 'protect women's sports' {cd_bowen}.

Says the schools 'must be run very efficiently' {cd_bowen}. In January 2026 he said the late-2025 insurance costs came from keeping premiums low, which left the corporation effectively self-insured once coverage ran out {cd_stifel}.

on_incumbent: Says he led the board through hiring the new superintendent; LaGrange was chosen from 12 applicants, seven of whom were interviewed {cd_bowen}{cd_hire}.
plans: Says he will set clear expectations for the administration and 'Inspect what I expect' {cd_bowen}.
gaps: No endorsements or campaign finance reports found.
No news account found explaining why he moved from the Spencer Township seat to the at-large race.

candidates.summary: Former West Clark superintendent who now works in sales for an education services company; parent of current students; running to change how the district is managed {cd_schenck}. Listed as a Republican {hc_gen_list}.
background: Former teacher and administrator: junior high math and Orleans third-grade teacher, Crawford County middle school principal, assistant superintendent at Tell City-Troy Township and Southwest Dubois County, West Clark superintendent (2015–2018) and chief operations officer (2018–2021) {cd_schenck}.
Lists his current job as senior account executive with Perfection Group since 2021 {cd_schenck}.
Holds education degrees from Indiana University and an education specialist degree from Oakland City University {cd_schenck}.
Parent of children who attend North Harrison schools {cd_schenck}.
path_to_ballot: Filed as a Republican for the Jackson Township seat; first run for elected office {hc_gen_list}{cd_schenck}.

items: Says he would propose cost-saving measures within 30 days that would not cut any teaching position, and believes $500,000 can be saved in the education fund {cd_schenck}.
Says the savings would pay for staff raises or stipends, offset enrollment declines and reduce transfers from the operations fund, freeing operations money for facility upgrades {cd_schenck}.
Says the district is losing teachers and that staff should be valued and respected {cd_schenck}.
Wants freed-up operations money to go to facility upgrades {cd_schenck}.

on_incumbent: Says board members and the superintendent have made serious errors in management and judgment and that he would hold leadership accountable {cd_schenck}.
Says politics has no place in board governance and that he would not let it enter his decisions {cd_schenck}.
plans: Says he has researched the tax rate, enrollment trends, staffing, facilities and inefficiencies and would bring proposals in his first 30 days {cd_schenck}.
gaps: No endorsements or campaign finance reports found.
He did not name specific cuts behind the $500,000 savings estimate in the questionnaire.

candidates.summary: Incumbent board member; appointed in September 2024 to fill a vacancy and now board secretary {cd_bowyer}{cd_stifel}. Listed as a Republican {hc_gen_list}.
background: Works for Consolidated Electrical Distributors; 1980 graduate of Jeffersonville High School and Prosser Vocational School {cd_bowyer}.
His three children are North Harrison graduates and three grandchildren attend the district {cd_bowyer}.
path_to_ballot: Appointed in September 2024 from a group of volunteers to fill a vacancy left by a resignation; filed as a Republican for the Jackson Township seat in 2026 {cd_bowyer}{hc_gen_list}.

items: Wants instruction focused on math, science, social studies, English, special education and career/agriculture programs {cd_bowyer}.
Lists finance and budget among the issues needing attention {cd_bowyer}. In October 2025 he told teachers asking for raises that the money is not there to pay teachers more {cd_pay}.
Lists declining enrollment and its effects as a priority {cd_bowyer}.
Acknowledges that not everyone who attends board meetings is convinced the district's special education programs are as good as they can be {cd_bowyer}.
Lists teacher and staff retention as a priority {cd_bowyer}.

Lists transparency with the public about school business as a priority {cd_bowyer}; said in January 2026 that 'the transparency that this board wants to parlay to you guys can't be overstated' {cd_stifel}.

on_incumbent: Says the current board is productive and 'has made and will continue to make real progress' {cd_bowyer}.
Voted with the full board for the classroom display policy; when asked at the Aug. 13 meeting to explain the vote, he said, 'Appreciate everyone's opinion. We have our own.' {cd_display}
plans: Says priorities shift and need simultaneous attention; lists enrollment, special education, staff retention, budget, student safety and transparency, in no set order {cd_bowyer}.
gaps: Fetched sources do not state which seat he was appointed to; a 2024 district vacancy notice for a Jackson Township seat was seen only in a search snippet (unverified), and 2022 Jackson Township winner Chris Lasley is not on the 2026 ballot.
No endorsements or campaign finance reports found.

candidates.summary: Pharmacist and health-care manager and parent of North Harrison students; first run for office, focused on the district's finances {cd_inboden}. Listed as an Independent {hc_gen_list}.
background: Principal for preferred drug list and supplemental rebate operations at MedImpact Healthcare Systems; holds a Doctor of Pharmacy from Purdue and an MBA from the University of Alabama at Birmingham {cd_inboden}.
Parent of children who attend or attended North Harrison {cd_inboden}.

Has volunteered as a youth sports coach and officer, a band booster and a volunteer assistant wrestling coach at the high school; the board approved him as a volunteer wrestling coach for 2026-27 {cd_inboden}{cd_crash}.
path_to_ballot: Filed as an Independent for the Jackson Township seat; no prior elected office {hc_gen_list}{cd_inboden}.

items: Says his top priority is helping the corporation stabilize and improve its finances as state changes reduce revenue {cd_inboden}.
Calls the Stifel financial review a good first step, and says the board and administration must keep developing and carrying out changes {cd_inboden}.
Wants to seek more resources through grant writing and partnerships while using current resources efficiently {cd_inboden}.

on_incumbent: Describes the board's 2026 partnership with Stifel as 'a great first step' {cd_inboden}.
plans: Cites nearly a decade of work with multimillion-dollar budgets and government regulations as preparation for analyzing district finances {cd_inboden}.
gaps: No endorsements or campaign finance reports found.
No stated positions found on curriculum, safety or the classroom display policy.

candidates.summary: Systems administrator making his first run for office; emphasizes academics and budgeting {cd_fanz}. Listed as a Republican {hc_gen_list}.
background: Works as a system administrator; holds a bachelor's degree in computer science {cd_fanz}.
Coached girls' team sports and served three years as president of a USA Swimming club {cd_fanz}.
path_to_ballot: Filed as a Republican for the Jackson Township seat; first run for elected office {hc_gen_list}{cd_fanz}.

items: Says schools should focus on reading, writing, mathematics, science and history, with high academic standards and an emphasis on discipline, respect and order {cd_fanz}.
Says schools should respect the role families play in shaping their children's values {cd_fanz}.
Wants to empower teachers to teach effectively {cd_fanz}.
Says he would work to keep budgets balanced and direct resources where they help students and teachers most {cd_fanz}.
Says taxpayers deserve transparency and responsible stewardship of public funds {cd_fanz}.

plans: Says his first priority would be keeping schools focused on academic achievement and minimizing distractions from classroom instruction {cd_fanz}.
gaps: No comments found on the current board's decisions.
No endorsements or campaign finance reports found.

candidates.summary: Unopposed for the Spencer Township seat, which Josh Bowen won in 2022 {hc_gen_list}{hc_2022}. Listed as a Republican {hc_gen_list}.
path_to_ballot: Filed as a Republican for the Spencer Township seat; the Corydon Democrat lists him as the only candidate {hc_gen_list}{cd_gencands}.
gaps: No background, positions or questionnaire found; the Corydon Democrat profiled only contested races.
No endorsements or campaign finance reports found.

review_flags.summary: At the Aug. 13, 2026 board meeting, resident Jordan Black said in public comment that Bowyer had told him the board is a 'self-serving board' and that members will enact their own personal agendas; the Corydon Democrat reported the claim as Black's account and did not report a response from Bowyer to that specific claim {cd_display}.
review_flags.note: A secondhand account of a private remark by one speaker (who shares a surname with at-large candidate Ashley Black); not confirmed by Bowyer.

review_flags.summary: In his Sept. 2026 Corydon Democrat questionnaire, Schenck said the district's focus should be servant leadership, 'not ridicule, nepotism and party politics,' and accused board members and the superintendent of mismanagement; he gave no specific examples, and no response from the board or superintendent was published {cd_schenck}.
review_flags.note: An unspecified nepotism claim against current officials; the profile text keeps only his general management criticism.
